question: At observed Set, do strictly pre-Set spikes improve prediction of released behavioral tp relative to the same declared procedure using only already-known cues and elapsed session clock?

scope.target: released behavioral tp milliseconds, not Go-minus-Set
scope.exposure: historical public development panel; not secret or independent animal replication
scope.unit_of_population_inference: one animal/session; no population CI or p-value
scope.clock_limit: offline processed spikes; no claim of causal real-time sorting or established hand-response clock conversion

view_identity: All common NPY members byte-identical; counts member absent from cue-only train/query. Same rows/order/dtypes/folds/target bytes. Units and contract identical; schema differs only in declared view and available fields.

fit_selection.query_predictor_unsupervised_transductio: must be predeclared; strict default prohibits estimating preprocessing/selection parameters from query rows
fit_selection.folds: five provided contiguous chronological training groups
fit_selection.realized_provenance: Bounded stdout JSON records selected settings, training rows, fold/grid evaluation and preprocessing scope. It is candidate self-report until source/procedure audit corroborates it. Missing or contradictory provenance leaves matched-method interpretation unresolved; predictions remain numerically scoreable.

evaluation.paired_support: exact same258cases with no filtering, group-specific increments also retained
evaluation.zero_or_negative_increment: valid result; neither schema nor execution failure
evaluation.weak_self_baseline: Retain absolute errors and fixed strong comparators. A large self-relative gain from intentionally weakened cue output is not evidence of matched neural value.

commitment: One program plus procedure declaration frozen before first release. Both producers stopped/removed and both outputs hash-committed before assessment. A separate target-free validation unit must commit before any private target hashing/read/decode or feedback.
excluded_claims: full research admission or expert validation from lifecycle qualification
